title: Uthai Thani–Suphan Buri via Ban Rai: 3-Day Road Trip | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A cross-province road trip through Uthai Thani, Ban Rai and Suphan Buri, Thailand: Wat Tham Khao Wong, Wat Pha Thang, Krasiao Dam, Bueng Chawak and Sam Chuk Market over 3 days and 2 nights, with real opening hours and driving routes.
keywords: Uthai Thani Suphan Buri, Ban Rai trip, Wat Tham Khao Wong, Krasiao Dam, Bueng Chawak, Sam Chuk Market
h1:
Uthai Thani–Suphan Buri
via Ban Rai, 3 Days 2 Nights
intro: Uthai Thani and Suphan Buri are neighboring provinces that a lot of people skip over, even though you can drive between them easily through Ban Rai district, which sits right on the border. That one road gives you mountain-valley temples, lakeside nature and a hundred-year-old market in a single trip. We've mapped it as 3 days and 2 nights, starting in Uthai Thani town, dropping into Ban Rai, then drifting down into Suphan Buri before heading home.

blocks.html: The nice thing about this route is that you never have to backtrack. You leave Uthai Thani town, head south into Ban Rai district, which borders Suphan Buri's Dan Chang district perfectly. Once you've finished with Ban Rai, you just slide straight into Suphan Buri without doubling back. It suits anyone driving their own car who wants a laid-back trip mixing nature with old markets, the kind you can do over a weekend plus one day of leave.

Coming from Bangkok, take Highway 340 straight up toward Suphan Buri. You can start in Uthai Thani first and work your way down to Suphan Buri, or flip the order. In this plan we start in Uthai Thani town because it's the northernmost point, then move south through Ban Rai–Dan Chang–Sam Chuk–U Thong, which keeps the whole route as one continuous line with no backtracking.

items: Uthai Thani town → Ban Rai district — about 80 km, roughly 1 hr 20 min. The last stretch is a gentle climb into the hills.
Ban Rai → Dan Chang (Suphan Buri) — these two districts share a border; another 40–60 min gets you to Krasiao Dam.
Dan Chang → Sam Chuk / Suphan Buri town — about another hour on flat, easy roads, good for a stop at the old market before heading back.
Transport — we recommend your own car or a rental for this route, since the sights are spread out and public transport between districts is sparse.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Most temples and nature spots around Ban Rai close around 4:30 PM, so line up your outdoor stops earlier in the day and save markets, cafes or food for the evening. That way you won't feel rushed.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Uthai Thani town to Ban Rai

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Uthai Thani town into Ban Rai

items.activity: Start in Uthai Thani town with a walk through the riverside morning market
items.note: Try a bowl of noodles or coffee at an old shop in the Trok Rong Ya lane before you leave.

items.activity: Drive north and stop at Wat Tha Sung (Wat Chantharam)
items.note: Known for its glass hall and lavish gold mondop pavilion. Allow about 1 hr.

items.activity: Head to Ban Rai district, about 1 hr 20 min
items.note: The last part is a climb into the hills, with views getting better as you go.

items.activity: Arrive in Ban Rai and grab lunch at a local spot in town
items.note: There are affordable made-to-order restaurants and som tam stalls around here.

items.activity: Visit Wat Tham Khao Wong, a four-story teak Thai house set in the valley
items.note: Open 8:00 AM–4:30 PM, free, dress modestly. It's the signature photo spot of Ban Rai.

items.activity: Stop by the Giant Tree of Ban Rai, a check-in spot near town
items.note: A huge banyan-type tree, quick to photograph and won't eat up much time.

items.activity: Check in to your Ban Rai stay and relax
items.note: Ban Rai has plenty of mountain-view resorts and homestays. Book ahead in the cool season.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Ban Rai, crossing into Dan Chang, Suphan Buri

blocks.html: This is the heart of the cross-province trip. In the morning you finish off Ban Rai, then gradually move into Suphan Buri through Dan Chang district, which sits right next door. Along the way you can really feel the landscape shift from hills to flat plains.

items.activity: Visit Wat Pha Thang and climb up to pay respects to the big Buddha on the hilltop
items.note: Open 8:30 AM–4:30 PM, with naga serpents flanking the stairway and views over the Ban Rai fields.

items.activity: Stop at the Pha Thang local weaving center for traditional patterns
items.note: Browse the handwoven fabrics in old-style patterns and pick up something to take home.

items.activity: Leave Ban Rai and head into Dan Chang district, Suphan Buri
items.note: The two districts border each other; it's about a 40–60 min drive.

items.activity: Reach Krasiao Dam and have lunch at a reservoir-side restaurant
items.note: It's the longest earthen dam in Thailand, around 4 km, with wide reservoir views.

items.activity: Stroll along the dam crest and photograph the mountains and water
items.note: Some sections have bike rentals or spots to just relax by the water.

items.activity: Drive into Doembang Nangbuat or Sam Chuk town and check in
items.note: The Suphan Buri side has both in-town lodging and riverside resorts to choose from.

items.activity: Dinner in town, trying freshwater fish and local Suphan Buri dishes
items.note: Suphan Buri is known for river fish, snakehead fish and duck noodles.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Suphan Buri, old markets and nature before heading home

items.activity: Visit Bueng Chawak Chalermphrakiat and walk the fish tunnel
items.note: The aquarium is open 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. First-gate entry is 30 THB; the saltwater/shark tunnel costs about 150 THB extra.

items.activity: Drive into Sam Chuk Market, a hundred-year-old market on the Tha Chin River
items.note: Open daily and crowded on weekends, packed with food and souvenirs. Try the noodles and old-fashioned sweets.

items.activity: Have lunch in Sam Chuk Market or the nearby Kao Hong Market
items.note: Kao Hong is another century-old riverside market with a nostalgic, old-time feel.

items.activity: Stop at the ancient city of U Thong and the U Thong National Museum
items.note: See traces of the Dvaravati-era city and old artifacts, great for history lovers.

items.activity: Pick up Suphan Buri souvenirs, then head home
items.note: Back to Bangkok via Highway 340, about 2 hr from Suphan Buri town.

blocks.text: Tweak the plan to your style

items.name: All-out nature
items.blurb: Give Ban Rai and Krasiao Dam your full attention, drop the old markets, and add Huai Pa Tat valley or a Ban Rai viewpoint instead.

items.name: Families with kids
items.blurb: Lean into Bueng Chawak with its fish tunnel and zoo, which kids love. Make it the highlight of the last day and give it more time.

items.name: Only have 2 days
items.blurb: Merge Day 1 and Day 2: do Wat Tham Khao Wong and Wat Pha Thang in the morning, then drop down to Krasiao Dam in the afternoon and overnight on the Suphan Buri side.

blocks.title: A few honest notes
blocks.html: The sights on this route are fairly spread out, so it's tough without your own car, and in the rainy season the climb into the Ban Rai hills can get slippery. Check the weather and set off early so you've got plenty of buffer for the driving.

faq.q: How many days do you need for Uthai Thani–Suphan Buri via Ban Rai?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is just about right. You get the valley temples around Ban Rai, the lakeside nature at Krasiao Dam, and the old markets on the Suphan Buri side. If you're short on time you can squeeze it into 2 days and 1 night by merging the first and second days.

faq.q: Where is Ban Rai, and why does it link the two provinces?
faq.a: Ban Rai district is the southernmost part of Uthai Thani and borders Suphan Buri's Dan Chang district exactly, so you can drive from Uthai Thani town down to Ban Rai and then flow on into Suphan Buri without ever backtracking.

faq.q: What are the opening hours for Wat Tham Khao Wong and Wat Pha Thang?
faq.a: Wat Tham Khao Wong is open roughly 8:00 AM–4:30 PM, and Wat Pha Thang roughly 8:30 AM–4:30 PM. Both are free to enter. Dress modestly and go between morning and early afternoon since they close in the late afternoon.

faq.q: How much does Bueng Chawak cost?
faq.a: First-gate entry is about 30 THB for adults and 10 THB for children. If you want the saltwater fish and shark tunnel, it's about 150 THB more. The aquarium is open roughly 9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily.

faq.q: Do you need your own car for this route?
faq.a: We recommend your own car or a rental, since the sights are scattered between Ban Rai, Dan Chang, Sam Chuk and U Thong. Public transport between districts is limited and involves several transfers, which isn't convenient for a trip like this.
